Welcome. I’m really glad you’re here, because together, we’re about to dive into a conversation that’s shaped not just societies, but the lives and experiences of countless people—yours and mine included. You know, when we talk about racism, where it came from, and the fight to break it down, it can feel overwhelming. But what if we could peel back the layers and really see how these ideas about race took hold, how they’ve been challenged, and what’s kept them alive for so long?
That’s what we get to do with Stamped: Racism, Antiracism, and You, written by Jason Reynolds. Through powerful storytelling, he takes us on a journey through America’s past—showing us how racist thinking was built, how it’s been fought, and the moments that changed everything. We’ll walk alongside the people and movements that made choices—sometimes upholding injustice, sometimes pushing back against it with incredible courage. As we move from the earliest days of colonization right up to the present, we’ll start to see just how closely connected the past is to our world today. Every story, every turning point, weaves together to reveal not just the roots of prejudice, but also the hope and determination of those who refuse to accept it.
And here’s what makes this journey matter: exploring antiracism isn’t just about history. It’s an invitation to look at our own beliefs, to ask tough questions about the world around us, and to imagine what we could change if we truly understood the forces at work.
So, as we step into these pages together, let’s stay curious, open, and ready to see what’s possible. Because each chapter isn’t just a lesson—it’s a call to action for all of us.
